coverage: Four selected energy-relevant families; not a global assertion about every family.
classificationPolicy: A shared word, channel or model does not establish an identical theorem target. External theorem statements are recorded as publisher claims; this lane has not independently audited their full proofs.

records.title: Generalized amplitude-damping classical capacity
records.ourResult: Single-qubit ergotropy, passive energy and energy closure after zero-temperature amplitude damping followed by dephasing; finite numerical validation.
records.claimedExternalResult: Single-letter unrestricted classical capacity and repeated-use Holevo additivity for every generalized amplitude-damping channel; paper additionally claims additivity with any finite-dimensional partner channel.
records.exactModelMap: A_gamma,nu maps excited population p to (1-gamma)p+gamma*nu and coherence c to sqrt(1-gamma)c. Our pre-dephasing channel is the nu=0 special case.
hypotheses: Qubit density matrix, 0<=gamma,nu<=1; nu is stationary EXCITED population.
Memoryless identical channel uses; arbitrary entangled block inputs and collective decoding permitted.
Unassisted communication: no pre-shared entanglement or feedback.
missingPremisesOrWork: No Holevo information objective, input ensemble optimization, decoder, or n-use entangled channel analysis exists in our code.
Our ergotropy is a different functional of a prepared state. Extra dephasing is a composition outside the exact displayed channel unless separately treated.
records.transfer: Add generalized thermal damping and signed reservoir heat to our fixed-Hamiltonian qubit model, independently of capacity claims.
records.formalizationScope: Publisher scope doc lists repeated-use capacity/additivity and scalar attained maximum; expressly excludes additivity with arbitrary different partner and separate-measurement decoding. No Lean proof was run here.

records.title: Entropy photon-number inequality
records.ourResult: Two-dimensional qubit energy and ergotropy; no bosonic Fock-space beam splitter or entropy-power theorem.
records.claimedExternalResult: For n modes of each independent input into a passive beam splitter, entropy photon number of output C is at least eta*N(rho_A)+(1-eta)*N(rho_B), where N(rho)=g^{-1}(S(rho)/n).
hypotheses: n is a finite positive integer; both inputs have finite mean number.
Input is rho_A tensor rho_B: independence across the two ports; entanglement within either n-mode input is allowed.
g(x)=(x+1)log(x+1)-x log(x), distinct from the determinant-entropy function used in family 276.
missingPremisesOrWork: No bosonic channel or receiver encoding is specified by the project.
A physical mode identification, measured input noise, cross-port independence and numerical cutoff/tail error would all need justification.
records.transfer: Possible future thermal-noise bounds for an explicitly modeled bosonic receiver; entropy photon number is not output energy created without an input.
records.formalizationScope: Publisher scope document selects the EPnI itself; thermal-attenuator and broadcast-capacity consequences are outside that selected formalization. No Lean proof was run here.

records.title: Global classical relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell solutions
records.ourResult: Driven fixed-mutual-inductance RLC circuits coupled to one mechanical mode; finite linear ODE/phasor energy identity.
records.claimedExternalResult: Global unique classical solutions for the 3D one-species relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system with arbitrary-size smooth compatible initial data in the stated class.
hypotheses: Nonnegative f0 smooth and compactly supported in phase space R^3_x times R^3_v.
E0 and B0 are smooth with bounded derivatives and square-integrable, satisfying div E0=rho_f0 and div B0=0.
Relativistic velocity v/sqrt(1+|v|^2); collisionless one-species plasma, no background charge.
Conclusion is smoothness on every finite time interval and compact phase-space support there; no smallness, symmetry or neutrality premise.
missingPremisesOrWork: Our lumped finite-dimensional reciprocal circuit is not this kinetic PDE and has no phase-space distribution or Maxwell initial-value problem.
A solution-existence result neither supplies an uncounted source nor predicts a circuit conversion efficiency.
records.transfer: Keep as a distinct mathematical-physics node; do not attach a solved-by-us or energy-gain edge. Low priority for current tabletop protocol.
records.formalizationScope: Scope document describes this selected global-existence theorem; proof not executed or independently audited in this lane.

records.title: Two-dimensional ground-state area law
records.ourResult: Single prepared qubit with fixed Hamiltonian, not an interacting two-dimensional ground-state family.
records.claimedExternalResult: Entanglement entropy is bounded by C times boundary size for unique uniformly gapped ground states of bounded finite-range square-lattice Hamiltonians.
hypotheses: Finite induced square-lattice domain; local dimension q fixed.
One self-adjoint term per nonempty support X, graph diameter <=R and norm <=J; internal graph distance matters for domains with holes.
Unique ground state Omega and assumed global spectral gap Delta>0: H-E0*I >= Delta*(I-|Omega><Omega|).
The bound constant depends on q,R,J,Delta, not domain size or shape.
missingPremisesOrWork: No such many-body Hamiltonian, unique ground state or uniform gap has been established in our qubit energy work.
A spectral gap is an input hypothesis, so this theorem cannot establish the missing Yang–Mills gap.
The associated PEPS existence statement is not by itself an efficient numerical construction.
records.transfer: Conditional future tensor-network modeling after an independently justified many-body Hamiltonian and gap; no present theorem overlap.
records.formalizationScope: Not assessed in this lane; no family-wide verified badge is inferred.
